concepts.definition: Gardner's claim that human ability consists of several relatively independent intelligences.
The finding that tests of different cognitive abilities correlate positively.
A single factor behind the correlations between cognitive tests, proposed by Spearman in 1904.
A claimed preference for a mode of instruction, for which matching has no adequate evidence.

questions.a: Linguistic, logical-mathematical, spatial, bodily-kinesthetic, musical, interpersonal, intrapersonal and naturalist.

questions.q: Why does the positive manifold count against the theory?
questions.a: If the intelligences were independent, scores in different areas would not correlate, but cognitive tests correlate positively.

questions.q: How do multiple intelligences differ from learning styles?
questions.a: Intelligences are kinds of ability, styles are preferences for how to receive information, and the style claim has no adequate evidence.
